title: ironbark-payments-pilot-call-notes
content:
Call: Ironbark Payments — Pilot intake / tech discovery
Date: 2025-09-18 11:00 PT (60m)
Attendees: Evelyn (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SWE), Lena (Ironbark Eng), Jude (Ironbark Product), Maria (Ironbark Security)

Purpose: quick intake to scope LLM usage for payments reconciliation and webhook enrichment. Customer wants low-friction pilot to prove accuracy and latency before committing to Dedicated or Private.

High-level ask from Ironbark:
- Use-case: Match inbound webhooks (transaction records) to ledger entries and extract normalized fields (merchant_id, amount_usd, reconciliation_tag, probable_reason). Also generate short evidence summary to attach to each auto-matched transaction.
- Expected workload for pilot: ~200 req/s average, spike to 1k req/s for 2–4 minute bursts (end-of-day reconciliation). Typical input size: 120–600 tokens (webhook JSON + recent ledger context). Output size: 60–180 tokens.
- SLO target: p95 end-to-end < 500 ms for 90% of requests; acceptable fallback to p95 < 1.2s under burst if we trigger degrade policy.
- Data requirements: PCI-adjacent (no raw PANs in upstream), PII present (names, last4). Must be able to run in VPC or on-prem for production. Pilot ok with hosted but needs clear path to private.

Quick technical constraints flagged by Ironbark:
- Strict idempotency & ordering: webhook replay could happen; model outputs must be deterministic enough to support reconciliation idempotency checks.
- Numeric fidelity: amounts must not be hallucinated or rounded incorrectly (important for downstream accounting). Quantized models that change numeric formatting could be an issue.
- Long-context: They want to include last 8 ledger entries (+ webhook) as context to improve matching; that increases average sequence length and KV cache behavior matters.
- Throughput vs latency trade: prefer lower per-token cost but cannot compromise p95 too much.

Redwood notes / initial hypotheses:
- Serving model candidates: start with open LLM v1-large (baseline) and fallback to v1-small for degraded capacity. For numeric extraction accuracy, consider a dedicated extractors / regex post-processing layer to validate amounts extracted by model.
- Runtime config: conservative batching (target batch size 8–16) with strict latency cap to hit p95. For spikes use dedicated-burst routing to reserved dedicated nodes or autoscale policy.
- Caching: prefix caching of stable ledger context should give big wins (many webhooks reference same merchant/context). Recommend enabling KV cache warmup for pilot.
- Quantization: steer away from heavy 4-bit quantization for extraction models until numeric fidelity tests pass — recommend int8 or float16 in Dedicated proof.
- Routing policy: set policy that prefers private/dedicated instances when available, otherwise hosted variant with fallback to smaller model variant and degraded response (shorter summary + no non-critical fields).

Gotchas / risks surfaced in call:
- False positives in auto-match: tradeoff between recall for auto-match and manual review load. Need clear confidence score + audit trace for each decision.
- Prompt injection: webhooks may contain merchant-provided text fields — must sandbox and sanitize prompts, prefer structured templates and use tool-calling/structured output to reduce free-text ambiguity.
- Cold-starts: Their spike pattern (1k req/s bursts) could cause cold caches — suggest pre-warming during known windows (end-of-day). Discuss warm pool or scheduled warmup job.
- GDPR/DSAR: Even in pilot, Ironbark wants ability to purge specific customer traces. Hosted pilot must provide deletion controls or proof of data handling — otherwise pilot should run in their VPC.
- Observability: They want per-request token and cost breakdown surfaced to their engineers and product. Also need error traces for failed model calls.

Notes to self / reminders:
- Demo script should show: 1) high-precision extraction with regex fallback, 2) fallthrough to manual queue when confidence < threshold, 3) how caching reduces token usage (show before/after).
- Prepare quick benchmark: 120/300/600 token inputs with p95 latency + cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated (x86 GPU baseline). Include cost delta for int8 vs float16.
- Put together a short eval prompt set: 40 canonical webhook cases (mix clean, obfuscated, weird merchant fields) + 20 adversarial cases (prompt injection, malformed JSON, replayed webhooks).

Immediate action items (owner / ETA / tickets):
1) Evelyn: draft pilot checklist + config recommendations (model variants, batching, caching, fallback policy) — due 2025-09-23 — JIRA-PLT-879.
2) Samir: quick perf run using v1-large hosted profile (synthetic load at 200 req/s & 1k burst) + collect p95/p99 — due 2025-09-24 — link to infra PR when ready.
3) Lena (Ironbark): provide sample webhooks + 500 labeled examples (match / not-match / reason) by 2025-09-26 — will feed eval set.
4) Jude: confirm compliance boundary (can pilot run hosted with redacted PII?) — answer by 2025-09-22.
5) Maria (Ironbark Sec): want encryption-at-rest confirmation + KMS integration doc — Redwood to share references (Evelyn).

Bench sketch (quick handwritten calc)
- Average token input: 280 tokens; output 120 tokens -> ~400 tokens per request.
- At 200 req/s sustained -> 80k tokens/s -> 4.8M tokens/min -> cost rough estimate (placeholder) hosted ~ $X/min. Need precise numbers from pricing table.
- Caching expectation: 25–40% token reduction if prefix context reused.

Experiment ideas for pilot (brainstorm):
- Experiment A: Use structured extraction template + regex verification; fallback to LLM only for low-confidence items. Measure false positive rate reduction.
- Experiment B: Use a two-pass approach: cheap small embedding model to cluster candidate ledger rows, then call the LLM for final rich summary only for top-k matches (saves tokens).
- Experiment C: System prompt hardening + entity whitelist for numeric fields to prevent hallucinated merchants/amounts.

Meeting artifacts to prepare (Evelyn):
- Short one-pager: "Pilot runbook" including traffic profile, success criteria (precision/recall targets, latency), ops playbook for degrade + manual queue.
- Lightweight demo dataset & notebook showing caching effects and fallback behavior.
- Compliance FAQ: hosted vs VPC differences, KMS options, deletion support.

Loose thoughts / heuristics I jotted down:
- When in doubt, prefer deterministic post-processing (regex/float parse) for fields that feed accounting systems. LLM should provide context & human-readable reasoning, not the canonical amount.
- Try to keep model outputs in JSON schema + schema validation to avoid downstream parser flakiness. Use structured output mechanisms in Redwood API to reduce parsing errors.

Open questions for Ironbark (to confirm before pilot):
- Are we allowed redaction of last4 and names for hosted pilot? If not, we recommend VPC straight away.
- What is the target precision/recall for auto-match to consider pilot successful? (They said "meaningful reduction in ops load") — need numbers.
- Do they want on-device deterministic model for reconciliation (rare), or is a hybrid LLM+rules approach acceptable?

Next sync: schedule mid-pilot kickoff 2025-09-29 to review initial perf runs and ingest labeled data.

End of notes.

-- Evelyn
